items.evidence: After page.reload() (diff line 118) the test asserts rules toHaveCount(0) and the empty state (lines 124-125). Both would fail if the rule deletion never ran on the server.
Criterion 1 is asserted at lines 109-110. Criterion 2 is asserted after the reload: no rules (124-125), and the same promotion still loads, checked by URL, header and name input (121-123).
No existing page object covers promotions, and findPromotionId (lines 14-30) is a new lookup that follows the findOrderId pattern and reuses gql/adminToken. Nothing is duplicated.
There are no fixed waits; every wait is a web-first assertion.
test/expect come from ../../fixtures/test.ts (line 41), the test is untagged, it uses the orders scenario, and nothing writes to the cache or the dumps.
Everything is located by data-test-id or role, scoped to the rule card or the dialog. The one .first() (line 62) handles a test id that appears twice, and the comment says why.
The spec takes the promotion and its rule from the existing orders scenario and only reads the id through GraphQL.
No hard-coded ids: the promotion id is looked up by name at test time. The asserted values are the scenario's own data, not populatedb data.
The test uses the default admin actor through the fixture, with no UI login and no credentials in the spec.
typecheck.txt reports 'exit 0: no errors', and the spec is at e2e/tests/discounts/.

promotion-remove-rule.spec.ts lines 62-70 (diff lines 62-70) define every locator inline in the spec, and the delete/confirm flow (93, 105) is clicked inline instead of living on a new promotion page object in e2e/pages/.
The change adds no page object, so there is no page-object style to judge.
The test has // Arrange (56), // Act & Assert (90) and // Assert (115).
One test tells one story, with a test.step for each stage (91, 103, 116).
The title 'Removing the only rule leaves the promotion in place with no rules #e2e' describes the behaviour and carries the tag.
The comment block at lines 44-47 says what the spec covers and why it is untagged.
Every assertion is web-first (toHaveCount, toHaveText, toBeVisible, toHaveValue).
Line 87 types the literal "Channel-USD" instead of the scenario's exported CHANNEL.name.
There is no cleanup code and no random or unique names.
No per-test timeouts, retries, networkidle or waitForLoadState.
Relative imports keep the .ts extension, and nothing is imported from @playwright/test.
The gql call in findPromotionId is typed with a response generic, and there is no any and no cast.

Numbered step comments that restate the next line, such as '// 1. Open the "E2E Tee sale" promotion' (74), '// 4. Confirm by clicking "Delete" inside the dialog' (104) and '// 5. Reload the page' (117), narrate instead of explaining why.

structured_output.summary: The spec proves the outcome: after a reload, the promotion still loads and shows zero rules. It also uses the orders scenario, the fixture and a new read-only findPromotionId lookup, and it type-checks. All ten blockers are met. Three minors fail: every locator and action is written inline in the spec instead of on a promotion page object (M1); the channel name is a typed-in literal instead of CHANNEL.name (M8); and the numbered step comments narrate what the next line does (M13).
